RESEARCH / SAPA CENTRE

The research engine behind the ecosystem.

The Sports and Physical Activity (SAPA) Centre is GoSports' research and policy arm — advancing standards, measurement, and implementation pathways for a stronger, more coordinated sporting ecosystem in India.

Visit the SAPA Centre site
Where it comes from

Incubated by the Sports and Society Accelerator

The SAPA Centre was incubated in 2025 by the Sports and Society Accelerator (SSA) — a public-spirited, independent not-for-profit co-founded in 2022 by Nandan Kamath, GoSports Foundation's own Managing Trustee, together with Desh Gaurav Sekhri.

SSA works to strengthen the role of sport and physical activity in Indian society, convening government, civil society, philanthropy, academia, sport, health, and education around a more participative, outcomes-oriented approach. In 2025, SSA was recognised as a National Sports Promotion Organisation by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India.

Today the SAPA Centre is a dedicated vertical within GoSports. It serves as the central interface with the wider ecosystem, working towards universal participation and pathways to excellence, and advancing well-being, capability and national development.

The framework

The Sports Ecosystem Stack

Seven discrete, yet interconnected and non-hierarchical layers that are critical to a thriving sports ecosystem — recognising that sport is both a pathway to excellence and a public good in itself.

Excellence Layer

Medals · Process excellence

Governance Layer

Accountability · Stakeholder participation

Innovation Layer

Incentives · Platforms

Capacity Layer

Ecosystem-building · Return on investment

Policy Layer

Funding · Skill development

Knowledge Layer

Narrative · Social feedback loops

Participation Layer

Participant access · Non-participating contribution

This is the same framework GoSports refers to elsewhere on this site as the SAPA Stack — it underpins how we assess, shape, enable, and build across every programme.
